paras: The stoning of Paul Smith was an assault in Correville, a suburb of Cincinnati, Ohio, in which a man named John King threw stones at Smith, a Black man, and chased him until Smith choked him to death, probably in late July 1880. The only known account is a short wire brief that ran in a Kansas paper's crime column under the headline "Choked His Assailant to Death."

According to the brief, King stoned Smith until Smith turned and ran. King followed him, "pelting the colored man with rocks." Finding that he could not escape, Smith seized King, whom the brief called his "persecutor," by the throat and "literally choked him to death." The brief gives no date for the incident and does not state King's race or any reason for the attack.
No report of an arrest, inquest or trial appears in the coverage, and nothing shows whether Smith was charged with King's death.

The Topeka Tribune printed the story on August 5, 1880, in a "Criminalities" column of wire items, most of them dated July 23 to 29, alongside reports of a mob shooting in Moberly, Missouri, and an attack on a Black camp meeting near Hillsboro, Ohio. Its headline and the word "persecutor" placed the blame on King, but the brief treated the stoning as a joke, saying it went on "until the fun became monotonous to the African." No other white paper and no Black paper in the coverage carried the story.

accounts.gist: King stoned Smith and chased him throwing rocks until Smith, unable to escape, seized him by the throat and choked him to death.
